claim: AAAI 2026 accepted 'Incoherence' as a training-free, oracle-less measure that estimates a lower bound on whether an LLM-generated program is incorrect, without any reference implementation or test suite.
stance_target: what kind of code-correctness-estimation contribution AAAI accepts
quoted_support: we propose a measure of incorrectness, called incoherence, that can be estimated efficiently in the absence of an oracle and allows us to establish a lower bound on the error, i.e., the probability that the LLM-generated program for that specification is incorrect.

claim: Incoherence-based automatic detection identifies about two-thirds of incorrect programs with no reported false positives for the average task.
stance_target: headline empirical result quality bar at AAAI for code-correctness estimation
scope_conditions: average task across evaluated benchmark suite
quoted_support: our incoherence-based methodology can automatically identify about two-thirds of incorrect programs without reports of false positives for the average task.

claim: LLM rankings by pass@1 (oracle-based correctness) closely agree with LLM rankings by incoherence (oracle-less), implying oracle-based evaluation can be reliably replaced by an incoherence-based evaluation.
stance_target: feasibility of self-referential / no-ground-truth code correctness signals as an AAAI-worthy contribution
quoted_support: an oracle-based evaluation of LLMs can be reliably replaced by an incoherence-based evaluation. In particular, we find a very strong agreement between the ranking of LLMs by the number of programs deemed correct via an oracle (pass@1) and the ranking of LLMs by the number of programs deemed correct via incoherence.

claim: Incoherence targets whole-program binary correctness estimation, not per-requirement/per-test-case localization, unlike DPRC's per-requirement confidence.
stance_target: differentiation of DPRC's per-requirement localization novelty vs closest AAAI-accepted oracle-less code-correctness paper
quoted_support: can we somehow estimate how likely the generated program is correct?

claim: The Incoherence paper is training-free (a measure computed at inference time), whereas DPRC requires LoRA fine-tuning to elicit self-expressed per-requirement confidence.
stance_target: methodological contrast between two AAAI-adjacent code-correctness-estimation approaches
quoted_support: a measure of incorrectness, called incoherence, that can be estimated efficiently in the absence of an oracle
